title: One-Pot Pasta with Fresh Tomatoes
summary: The pasta cooks straight in the tomato sauce, a rustic method that gives a creamy dish and lets the pasta absorb all the flavour.

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large, wide pan over a medium heat. Add the sliced garlic, and the chilli flakes if using. Cook for {timer:1}, until fragrant; do not let the garlic brown.
Add the polpa pelati and crush any larger pieces with a wooden spoon. Season with salt and add some torn basil. Simmer for {timer:5} to develop the flavour.
Add the raw pasta straight to the sauce, stirring to coat each piece. Add just enough water or stock to cover the pasta; the liquid should be level with it.
Cook at a steady simmer, stirring often to stop it sticking and to release the starch. Add a splash of water whenever it looks dry. Cook for {timer:12-15}, until al dente.
When the pasta is al dente and the sauce clings nicely, take the pan off the heat. Stir in more fresh basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
Serve straight away with freshly grated Parmesan.

tips: Success depends on frequent stirring and adjusting the liquid. Use a wide pan so the pasta cooks evenly. Slice the garlic rather than mince it: the slices soften as they cook and give a milder, sweeter flavour. The starch the pasta releases is what makes the dish creamy.
